# opencode-kit

One command that installs, updates, or removes my [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugins.

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dhkimxx/opencode-kit/main/install.sh | bash
```

| Plugin | What it does | Release |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [opencode-lodestar](https://github.com/dhkimxx/opencode-lodestar) | Keeps OpenCode on track through compaction: puts your request, the agent's latest steps, and the files it was working on back after each compaction. `/lodestar off` and `/lodestar on` turn it off and on. | v0.4.2 |
| [opencode-ask](https://github.com/dhkimxx/opencode-ask) | Multi-turn side questions with `/ask`, in a full-screen panel that never adds to your conversation. | v0.3.3 |
| [opencode-delete](https://github.com/dhkimxx/opencode-delete) | Deletes the current session with `/delete`, after a confirmation. | v0.1.0 |

## What it does

- **Brings OpenCode to the version these releases were tested with.** An older OpenCode is upgraded with `opencode upgrade`. A newer one is left as it is, with a warning. If OpenCode is too old for the plugins and can't be upgraded, nothing is installed.
- **Installs each plugin at a fixed release**, such as `github:dhkimxx/opencode-ask#v0.3.3`, with `opencode plugin add`.
- **Removes every other copy first**, so nothing loads twice:
  - other entries for the same plugin in your settings, such as `github:dhkimxx/opencode-ask` without a release, or an older release;
  - clones in OpenCode's plugins folder, which move to `~/.config/opencode/opencode-kit-backup/`;
  - downloaded copies in OpenCode's cache. OpenCode reuses those when a plugin is added again, even if a newer version exists.

It changes OpenCode's settings only through `opencode plugin add` and `opencode plugin remove`, and leaves other plugins alone, including other people's plugins with the same names.

## Options

Pass options after `bash -s --`:

```sh
# Only some of the plugins
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dhkimxx/opencode-kit/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --only lodestar,ask

# Install the plugins, but leave OpenCode's version alone
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dhkimxx/opencode-kit/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --keep-opencode

# See what would change, without changing anything
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dhkimxx/opencode-kit/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --dry-run

# Remove the plugins
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dhkimxx/opencode-kit/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --uninstall
```

To update, run the install command again.

A running OpenCode picks up the changes within a few seconds. Restart it if a command such as `/ask` is missing.

## Requirements

- OpenCode 2.1.2 or newer. Tested with OpenCode 2.2.5, which an older OpenCode is upgraded to.
- Linux or macOS, with `bash` and `curl`. On Windows, use WSL, or install each plugin by hand as its README describes.

## Install by hand

Each plugin can still be installed on its own, for example:

```sh
opencode plugin add github:dhkimxx/opencode-ask#v0.3.3
```

Use one form of the name per plugin. OpenCode treats `github:dhkimxx/opencode-ask` and `github:dhkimxx/opencode-ask#v0.3.3` as two plugins, and `opencode plugin remove` only removes the exact name you give it.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are listed here.
This project follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org).

## [0.5.0] - 2026-11-01

### Changed

- `install.sh` installs opencode-lodestar v0.4.2, which keeps files in its restoration when their code doesn't all fit. opencode-ask stays at v0.3.3 and opencode-delete at v0.1.0, and OpenCode 2.2.5 is still the tested version.

## [0.4.0] - 2026-11-01

### Changed

- `install.sh` installs opencode-lodestar v0.4.1, which follows how OpenCode 2.2 sizes compaction. opencode-ask stays at v0.3.3 and opencode-delete at v0.1.0.
- An OpenCode older than 2.2.5 is upgraded to it. All three plugins were checked with OpenCode 2.2.5: opencode-ask and opencode-delete open in its TUI, and opencode-lodestar loads in its server. 2.1.2 is still the oldest version it accepts.

## [0.3.0] - 2026-10-29

### Added

- An OpenCode older than 2.2.0 is upgraded to it with `opencode upgrade`, before the plugins are installed. A newer OpenCode is left alone, and so is one that was uninstalled with `--uninstall`.
- `--keep-opencode` installs the plugins without upgrading OpenCode.

### Changed

- All three plugins were checked with OpenCode 2.2.0: opencode-ask and opencode-delete open in its TUI, and opencode-lodestar loads in its server. An OpenCode that is too old and can't be upgraded is still refused.

## [0.2.0] - 2026-10-24

### Changed

- `install.sh` installs opencode-lodestar v0.4.0, which adds `/lodestar on` and `/lodestar off`. opencode-ask stays at v0.3.3 and opencode-delete at v0.1.0. All three were checked with OpenCode 2.1.4, and 2.1.2 is still the oldest version it accepts.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-21

### Added

- `install.sh` installs opencode-lodestar v0.3.1, opencode-ask v0.3.3, and opencode-delete v0.1.0 with one command, and needs OpenCode 2.1.2 or newer.
- Before installing, it removes every other copy of these plugins: other entries in your settings, clones in OpenCode's plugins folder, and downloaded copies in OpenCode's cache.
- `--only` installs some of the plugins, `--uninstall` removes them, and `--dry-run` shows what would change.

# Releasing

## Versions

- Versions follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org).
- Every release is an annotated git tag named `vX.Y.Z`, made on `main`. A tag is never moved or reused.
- `main` is what the install command runs, so it is always ready to release. Work happens on branches and merges into `main` when it is ready.
- A release can be pinned by its tag: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dhkimxx/opencode-kit/v0.1.0/install.sh | bash`.

## When a plugin is released

1. In `install.sh`, update the plugin's release in `PLUGINS`. If the new set was tested with another OpenCode version, update `OPENCODE_TESTED`, and `OPENCODE_MIN` if a plugin now needs a newer OpenCode.
2. Update the table and requirements in `README.md`.
3. Release the kit as below. A new plugin release is a minor version of the kit.

## Steps

1. Update `KIT_VERSION` in `install.sh` and add a section for it to `CHANGELOG.md`.
2. Run the tests:

   ```sh
   bash test/test.sh                 # a real OpenCode, in throwaway folders; needs GitHub access
   bash test/compat.sh               # a stand-in OpenCode
   docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/w" -w /w bash:3.2 bash test/compat.sh   # the bash that macOS ships
   ```

   CI runs them on every push. Every Monday it also runs `test/test.sh` against the newest OpenCode, on Linux and macOS, and opens an issue when that fails.

3. Commit, for example `Release v0.2.0`, then tag and push:

   ```sh
   git tag -a v0.2.0 -m "v0.2.0"
   git push origin main v0.2.0
   ```

4. The Release workflow checks that the tag matches `KIT_VERSION` and creates a GitHub release with the notes from `CHANGELOG.md`.
